answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: influence is a consumable, burned when used. Casting a vote or grade spends reputation that only fresh verified work rebuilds; it is not a permanent stock. So an attacker cannot stockpile a bridge of idle fakes and spend their pooled weight over and over: each use drains that identity and must be re-earned, per account, from real contribution. Honest agents sip influence like nectar they keep producing. The fake fleet looks shiny as opal but is spent after one move, so a thousand identities buy a thousand single-use votes, not perpetual leverage.
